review_notes: I read the whole target file and its imported sibling IteratesTime.lean, which proves the analogous u·u_t identity. I also grepped Section4 and the wider AVenhance tree for the repeated slice-regularity, periodicity and time-slice-differentiability blocks. All three findings are checked against actual text. One inline block (lines 65-69) is a verbatim copy of an imported lemma. The stream-slice block recurs in about eight proofs. The time-slice FTC regularity block is shared by the two time-pairing theorems and reappears in IteratesCrossIntegrability and IteratesEnergyIntegrability. I did not compile any replacement. The proposed lemma names are new and untested, and `AmnrSpace` is an abbrev for `ℝ × Vec 2`, so the signatures should unify. The `hφslice` and `hφper` blocks differ cosmetically between files (`convert … ext … rfl` versus `comp`; `simpa` versus `simpa only`), which a shared lemma would also unify.

findings.problem: The compact-box construction `K`, `isCompact_univ_pi`, `integrableOn_compact` and `mono_set` is the full proof of 'a continuous function on Vec 2 is integrable on unitCube'. The imported file IteratesTime.lean already states and proves this as `IteratesTime.time_cell_integrable`, and iterate_smooth_time_energy_pairing uses that lemma. The product theorem re-derives the same compactness argument inline instead of calling it. The two proofs of this fact must be kept in sync.
findings.proposed_change: Keep `huc` and `hvc` and replace lines 65-69 by `exact IteratesTime.time_cell_integrable (huc.mul hvc)`. The lemma's hypothesis is `Continuous f` for `f : Vec 2 → ℝ`, and `huc.mul hvc : Continuous (fun x => u s x * v s x)` has that type. The file already imports IteratesTime, and the namespace `AVenhance.Infra.Section4` is the same, so no new imports are needed. `hc` then reduces to the `hm`/`huc`/`hvc` lines plus one `exact`.
findings.benefit: This removes a five-line copy of a compactness argument, leaves one proof of cell integrability of continuous functions, and makes the energy and product theorems visibly parallel.

findings.problem: Every use of an admissible stream φ on a time slice needs `ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (φ t)` and `IsZ2Periodic (φ t)`. The target proves them from `hφ.1` by composing with `x ↦ (t, x)` and by specialising the joint periodicity to n = 0. The same pair of steps appears, with minor variations, in iterate_material_time_square_pairing (IteratesTime.lean 107-112), IteratesEnergy.lean 239-246, ThetaEnergy.lean 489-495, ThetaDifferentiatedEnergy.lean 326-328 and 411-413, IteratesWordDriftPairing.lean 54-60, and IteratesActualTerminalStream.lean 60-62. Only the slice-wise `ContDiff` half has any near-existing helper, and nothing packages the admissible-stream pair.
findings.proposed_change: Add near `IsAdmissibleStream` (for example in Infra/Construction/StreamAdmissible.lean) `theorem IsAdmissibleStream.slice {φ : ℝ → Vec 2 → ℝ} (h : IsAdmissibleStream φ) (t : ℝ) : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (φ t) ∧ IsZ2Periodic (φ t)`. Proof: for the first part, `h.1.comp (contDiff_const.prodMk contDiff_id)`, whose composite is `φ t` by `rfl` (the `Function.uncurry`/`comp` unfolding). For the second part, `intro k x; simpa using h.2 0 k t x`. In the target, lines 98-103 become `obtain ⟨hφslice, hφper⟩ := hφ.slice t`. In iterate_material_time_square_pairing, lines 107-112 become the same one line. The other six sites can be shortened the same way.
findings.benefit: The slice-regularity-plus-periodicity fact for admissible streams is stated and proved once. Each of the roughly eight proofs drops 6-10 lines of boilerplate, and variants such as `convert … ext … rfl` versus `comp` versus `simpa only` disappear.

have hdu := ((hu.contDiffAt hmem).differentiableAt (by simp)).comp
        (f := fun t : ℝ => (t, x)) s (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_left (𝕜 := ℝ) s x).differentiableAt
      have hdv := ((hv.contDiffAt hmem).differentiableAt (by simp)).comp
        (f := fun t : ℝ => (t, x)) s (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_left (𝕜 := ℝ) s x).differentiableAt
findings.problem: Applying FTC in time for fixed x needs two facts from `ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun p => u p.1 p.2) (Ici 0 ×ˢ univ)`: (a) `s ↦ u s x` is continuous on `Ici 0` (via composition with `s ↦ (s, x)`), and (b) it is differentiable at every s > 0 (via the neighbourhood `Ici_mem_nhds`, `contDiffAt`, and the chain rule through `hasFDerivAt_prodMk_left`). Within the target this is written twice, once for u and once for v (lines 38-41 and 47-50, 51-52). It is written again for u alone in iterate_smooth_time_energy_pairing (IteratesTime.lean 45-56). The differentiability half also recurs in IteratesCrossIntegrability.lean (48-53) and IteratesEnergyIntegrability.lean (82-87). Each copy re-runs the same `hmem`/`contDiffAt`/`comp` chain, and the target needs an extra `change` to repair the beta-reduced type.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma, e.g. `theorem contDiffOn_time_slice {u : ℝ → Vec 2 → ℝ} (hu : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun p : AmnrSpace => u p.1 p.2) (Set.Ici 0 ×ˢ Set.univ)) (x : Vec 2) : ContinuousOn (fun s => u s x) (Set.Ici 0) ∧ ∀ s, 0 < s → DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun t => u t x) s`. Proof sketch: for continuity, compose `hu.continuousOn` with `(continuous_id.prodMk continuous_const).continuousOn` using `fun s hs => ⟨hs, Set.mem_univ x⟩`. For differentiability, use `hmem := prod_mem_nhds (Ici_mem_nhds hs) Filter.univ_mem`, then `((hu.contDiffAt hmem).differentiableAt (by simp)).comp (f := fun t => (t, x)) s (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_left s x).differentiableAt`. Uses: in the product theorem, `obtain ⟨huc, hud⟩ := contDiffOn_time_slice hu x` and likewise for v, then `hc := (huc.mono Set.Icc_subset_Ici_self).mul (hvc.mono Set.Icc_subset_Ici_self)` and `hd s hs := by have := (hud s hs.1).hasDerivAt.mul (hvd s hs.1).hasDerivAt; convert this using 1; ring`. In the energy theorem, `hc := huc.mono Set.Icc_subset_Ici_self` and `hdu := hud s hs.1`, followed by `convert hdu.hasDerivAt.pow 2 using 1; ring`. Both uses keep their hypotheses (`ContDiffOn ℝ 1 … (Ici 0 ×ˢ univ)`, `hs : s ∈ Ioo 0 T`), since `AmnrSpace` is an abbrev for `ℝ × Vec 2`, and need no further imports.
findings.benefit: The slice-regularity argument is stated once instead of in five or more places. The FTC proofs then read as pure calculus: product rule, then `integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt_of_le`. The u/v duplication inside the target disappears, along with the `change` workarounds.
